issues.legal_issue: A borrower who has already invoked the statutory remedy under the SARFAESI Act may not ordinarily bypass that remedy by seeking relief under Article 226 of the Constitution.

Confirmation of a sale under Rule 9(2) of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 gives the successful auction purchaser a vested right to obtain the sale certificate upon complying with the terms of payment.
Under the amended Section 13(8) of the SARFAESI Act, a borrower’s right to redeem the secured asset ends upon publication of the auction notice.
The amended Section 13(8) of the SARFAESI Act prevails over the general right of redemption under Section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.

A secured creditor that has confirmed a sale under Rule 9(2) and received the full bid amount must issue the sale certificate under Rule 9(6) and may not withhold it to enter into a private arrangement with the borrower.
A High Court exercising jurisdiction under Article 226 may not use equitable considerations to override the statutory outcome of an auction conducted under the SARFAESI Act.
Courts should protect the sanctity of a valid public auction and interfere with its outcome only on legally sufficient grounds.
The interpretation of amended Section 13(8) adopted in Concern Readymix, Amme Srisailam, and Pal Alloys does not state the correct position of law.
